newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rise in active trade by lunch break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rise in active trade by lunch break.

text.p: Thai stocks gained in active trade by the lunch break on Tuesday as investors bought stocks as they waited to see if the government would take loans from the IMF in addition to seeking its advice, brokers said.

"Investors are watching whether the government would ask for loans from the IMF besides seeking its advice to solve the country's ailing economy. Everybody wants to see the outcome quickly but this issue is rather a delicate matter," said Witawus Charuchandr of Ekachart Finance.
The composite SET index rose 9.40 points, or 1.38 percent, to 690.07 on 5.05 billion baht turnover by lunch.
Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Monday he would meet IMF officials this week to seek advice on how to tackle the Thai economic crisis.
Brokers said Rerngchai's resignation had little impact on the market which had expected the move.
Nava Finance topped the active list, gaining 1.50 baht to 33.50, Thai Farmers Bank slipped one to 123, and PTT Exploration shed four to 430.
